lines.english: "A lot of rain we're having."
"Apparently it's going to be like this the whole weekend. That's what the weather report said."
"Come to think of it, Japan should be entering its rainy season right about now."
"…It is?"
"You still don't like talking about Japan?"
"No… I don't really mind."
There's my mom, who still has lingering affection for Japan, and then there's me, who's abandoned even the notion of remembering Japan.
Whenever the topic of that country comes up, we lose sight of our conversation.
"Hey, Kazusa."
"What?"
"If you look out the window, there's a single large tree, right?"
"Yeah, what about it?"
"When that tree loses all of its leaves, I'll be…"
"It's the beginning of summer and it's raining. That thing will only grow more leaves for a good while."
"It'll be fine until winter, at least."
Despite all that, mom keeps fighting on when she's spending time with me, continuing to play the role of "Touma Youko" as she always has.
But when mom does that, even I can clearly tell that she's fighting.
And that's not all…
The enjoyable period at the start of every visit has been getting shorter and shorter.
She's lost weight. She's eating less. Day by day, I notice her arms and legs grow thinner.
Day by day, she gets slightly paler. Even the shine in her hair and skin have gone away.
…And above all, she's started to neglect even hiding that fact.
"You know about the safebox furthest inside the living room closet, right?"
"We had something like that?"
"We do. Anyway, the key to that safe is inside the drawer of the buddhist altar."
"You came all the way to Vienna to pray to Buddha…?
Wait, we have a buddhist altar?"
"You were supposed to laugh, you know."
"Ah, aah…"
"It's actually in the top drawer next to my bed."
"Right."
"Anyway, once you've opened the safe using that key, you'll find the key to a bank vault…"
"There are already too many keys."
"But the bank vault requires a PIN on top of the key. I'll tell you the code now so listen properly. Don't ever think of writing it down; memorize it."
"Just forget about it. It sounds like a pain."
"Memorize it. You'll need it when the time comes."
"I told you, I have no interest in property or entitlements. You already know that, Mom."
"Well, now's the time to start getting interested. You'll inherit Touma Youko Office someday… Or well, it'll be Touma Kazusa Office by then, I guess."
"I don't really need it. If I ever lose the ability to play the piano, I'll just drop dead by the roadside or something. I wouldn't really mind a life like that."
"You can't. You absolutely can't! Even if you end up alone, you absolutely must live a happy life."
"Money can't buy happiness. You should know that better than anyone, Mom…"
"Perhaps that's true, but no one drops dead by the roadside out of happiness. So please listen to me."
"Mom…"
And even once the enjoyable period at the start is over, Mom remains talkative.
She's clearly tearing away at her body, her energy, in an attempt to feign indifference, but it's all too obvious.
A time unlike anything that has come before, one filled with terrible sadness for meーI'm talking with my mom, but I'm not enjoying it at all.
She's not making fun of me anymore. She's not avoiding confrontations anymore.
She's been talking more and more about her regrets, worries and memories.
It's almost as if the person I'm talking to has ceased to be Touma Youko…
"Hey, Kazusa…"
"Hm?"
"Do you want to hear about your dad?"
"No, I'd rather not."
"Why not?"
"I don't care anymore, that's all."
"But if I were to… If you were to end up all alone in this world…"
"No matter what my future holds in store, my one and only parent is Touma Youko."
"Kazusa…"
I also feel somewhat guilty over being the sole descendant of Touma Youko, for that matter.
"So just stop with these what-if talks. I've said this a hundred times already, but I don't regret anything, and I don't hate or resent you at all, Mom."
"Kazusa…!"
"…Just stop it already."
"I'm sorry, Kazusa… for not being able to leave anything for you…! Haah……gh…!"
Mom's weeping breaks the silence of the hospital room, resounding amidst the pitter-patter of the rain outside.
"I told you to stop."
I didn't say that out of embarrassment. I really wanted her to stop.
Because this is just too painful.
Seeing the confident and easygoing person who was my mom… slowly break apart.
Because it means that…
Whether she's still alive or not, the very existence that is Touma Youko is already on the path to a slow death.
Touma Youko was always an arrogant goddess in my eyes. She was a selfish mother. She was an insurmountable wall of a rival.
But the person in front of me right now is just a normal person. A calm old woman trying to give guidance to the young.
This isn't the Touma Youko I, or the world, has come to desire…
"Hey, Mom. Hurry up and get discharged from this place…"
So, unable to handle this atmosphere any longer, I make an unreasonable demand of someone who's supposed to be weaker than me.
"Then I'll let you hear me playing the piano. I've gotten much better since my last concert, you know?
Because I'm still weak too.
Because I'm still a little kid chasing her mother's shadow. It's not something I can move on from at the drop of a hat.
"What do you prefer? Beethoven? Schubert? Mozart? I'll play any request you have."
"So please, please… stop making me so sad…"
"…Cloture."
At that moment…
With slightly tearful eyes, Mom looks up at me and mutters…
"I'd like to hear Cloture."
A piece so obscure that I imagine not even classical music enthusiasts can immediately recognize it.
The composer, the period, the original name; all unknown.
Even the name Cloture was given by those who, without evidence, said that the piece originated in France.
The Germans have a completely different name for itーDie andere Seite des Glucksーand claim that their country is the true origin.
And I'm familiar with both names.
"It's the first piece I ever played here in Europe… It's the piece I've played more than any other in my lifetime."
Because it's the song my mom knows better than any other… and more than anything…
"It's a concerto, right?"
It's a piano concertoーa performance that requires an accompanying orchestra.
In other words, I'd have to either hold a concert of my own, or hire an orchestra…
It's not a piece I can play by myself. It's something that requires the help of many others.
